walkthroughs.body_html:
Judaism: The Patriarchs & Early Leaders — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Judaism: The Patriarchs & Early Leaders brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Judaism: The Patriarchs & Early Leaders.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why do Jews not accept Jesus as the Messiah?
options: Because the Jewish Messiah is expected to bring peace, rebuild the Temple and restore Israel — events the Jewish tradition holds Jesus did not accomplish.
Because Jews believe Jesus never existed.
The Torah is a single scroll containing every Jewish text.
Because Jesus was crucified, and the Messiah cannot die.
The first five books of the Hebrew Bible (Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy) — traditionally attributed to Moses and containing law, narrative and covenant.
Because Jesus was crucified, and the Messiah cannot die.
The Torah is a single scroll containing every Jewish text.
The Torah is the same as the Book of Genesis.

mcqs.q: What does the Abrahamic covenant in Judaism involve?
options: The covenant means Jews must not interact with non-Jews.
God's promise to Abraham of land, descendants and blessing, in return for faithfulness — the foundational covenant marking Jews as a covenant people with responsibilities, not privileges.
The Torah is a single scroll containing every Jewish text.
Being 'chosen' means Jews believe they are superior to other peoples.
